# At a glance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Format | Standard (Reality Fracture, set code `fra`, plus basic lands) |
| Colors | Blue, black, green (Sultai); Twinned Vision is hybrid blue and cast for `{1}{U}` |
| Archetype | Surveil / graveyard-mill engine with two flashback-style payoffs |
| Size | 60 cards: 24 lands, 36 spells |
| Primary win | Recursive Recruitment flashed back: two Cadet tokens that enter with `+1/+1` counters equal to a third of your graveyard |
| Secondary win | Tarmogoyf, Dark Matter Manipulator and Winter, Tormented Loner beat down while Hall of Echoes copies the biggest attacker |
| Land as engine | Hall of Echoes turns into a copy of your largest creature for `{5}`, adding a lethal body and ignoring the legend rule |
| Average mana value | 2.8 |

# Overview

Reality Fracture's surveil axis is not a card-selection theme, it is a fuel line. Forty-three cards in the set surveil and
forty-nine reference the graveyard, and the strongest of them convert library-to-graveyard movement into size. This deck
takes that literally: every spell either fills the graveyard, profits from the graveyard, or both. There is no card in the
sixty that does neither.

The cheapest engine is **Dark Matter Manipulator** (`{B}`, 1/2). It mills three on entering and gains `+2/+0` for every
seven cards in your graveyard, so once the fuel is flowing it stops being a one-drop and becomes a four- or six-power
attacker for one mana. Two more mill effects sit on bodies: **Something Worth Saving** (`{1}{G}` instant, mill four, take
a permanent from among them, gain 1 life) and **Primal Witchstalker** (`{1}{B}{G}`, 2/1 menace, mill four and return a
land from the graveyard to the battlefield tapped). **Seasoned Cryomancer** (`{1}{U}{U}`, 2/2) filters two cards into the
graveyard and taps down the opponent's board for each nonland card discarded, then exiles itself to draw two later.

The payoff side is where the deck stops being a mill pile. **Recursive Recruitment** (`{2}{U}{B}`) makes two 2/2 Cadets,
and its flashback halves the cost of the second cast by putting the card in the graveyard first: cast from a graveyard,
each Cadet enters with a `+1/+1` counter for every three cards in your graveyard. **Tarmogoyf** (`{1}{G}`) and
**Winter, Tormented Loner** (`{2}{B}`, 0/3) scale off the same number. **Uldaros Theorix** (`{3}{U}{B}{B}`, 5/5 flier)
exiles one nonland card of each type from the graveyard, copies them, and lets you cast up to six mana of those copies for
free. **Cruel Calculations** (`{2}{U}`) draws a card for every card that hit a graveyard from a library this turn, which
in this deck means it draws four off one mill spell.

There is no ramp and no fixing beyond the set's own duals: the curve tops out at six and the deck wants to spend turns
one through four developing, milling and attacking.

# Approach

## Game plan phases

| Phase | Turns | What you are doing |
|---|---|---|
| Seed | 1–3 | Land a Manipulator or Witchstalker, mill six to eight cards, find a Tarmogoyf or a Cryomancer |
| Fuel | 3–5 | Something Worth Saving and Cryomancer push the count past fifteen; Chandra surveils every turn and rebuys noncreature spells |
| Convert | 4–6 | Recursive Recruitment in hand or in the graveyard, Sphinx of False Conclusions trading into a token copy, Uldaros Theorix refilling |
| Close | 5+ | Flashback Recruitment for two large Cadets, copy the biggest body with Hall of Echoes, swing with flying and menace |

## Card roles

| Role | Cards | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mill / surveil | Dark Matter Manipulator, Something Worth Saving, Primal Witchstalker, Chandra, Chill of Compliance | 13 | Manipulator and both mill spells are the floor of the engine; Chandra surveils every turn for free |
| Graveyard scaling | Tarmogoyf, Winter, Tormented Loner, Darklight Phoenix | 7 | Goyf counts card types across all graveyards, Winter counts creature and planeswalker cards in yours |
| Card flow | Seasoned Cryomancer, Twinned Vision, Cruel Calculations, Sphinx of False Conclusions | 12 | Cryomancer and Sphinx discard, which is milling with upside; Twinned Vision draws two when cast from the graveyard |
| Token payoff | Recursive Recruitment, Sphinx of False Conclusions | 5 | Recruitment is the primary win; the Sphinx leaves a copy behind when it dies |
| Free-cast payoff | Uldaros Theorix | 2 | Exiles one card of each type from the graveyard and casts the copies for free, up to six mana |

## Lands as engines

| Land | Role in the deck |
|---|---|
| Hall of Echoes | The sixth mana sink and the second win condition. `{5}` turns it into a copy of Tarmogoyf, a Cadet or Uldaros for a turn, and the legend rule is switched off so two Uldaros can attack |
| Transformative Commons | Green and blue for free when a planeswalker is out; Chandra is a planeswalker, so two of four copies usually enter untapped |
| Formidable Commons | Black and green, same planeswalker clause |
| Theorix Annex | Blue and black, same clause |
| Shipwreck Marsh | Blue and black, untapped once you have two other lands |
| Room of Refuge | Any colour on turn one, and a `{5}` sacrifice mode that puts two `+1/+1` counters on a flier |

## Curve and mana

Twenty-four lands, thirteen blue sources, twelve green, eleven black; the only double-colour costs are blue
(`{1}{U}{U}` on Cryomancer, Chandra and Sphinx) and the fixed `{3}{U}{B}{B}` on Uldaros. The one-drop slot is four
Manipulators, the two-drop slot has eleven cards, and everything above four is two Uldaros. Four Islands, four Swamps and
four Forests mean the deck functions after a wipe on lands alone, which matters because the duals all want a planeswalker
or two other lands first.

# Gameplay strategy

## Early game

Lead on a Manipulator when you have one: it mills three immediately, which turns on Goyf's card-type count and starts
the graveyard clock. Hold Something Worth Saving until you can use the permanent it returns; milling four on turn two to
find nothing is still fine, but the card is at its best when it rebuys a Recursive Recruitment or a Chandra you already
used. Primal Witchstalker is the turn-three play that guarantees a fourth land, since it returns a land from the graveyard
to the battlefield tapped.

## Mid game

Chandra, Chill of Compliance is the engine's steering wheel. Her first `+1` surveils and returns any noncreature,
nonland card you bin to your hand, so every Chandra activation is either a free spell back or a land on top; her second
`+1` pays for the noncreature spell you just rebought. Seasoned Cryomancer is the other half: draw two, discard two, and
tap down two attackers in the process. Against creature decks that sequence is often a two-for-one on defence, and it
sets up Cruel Calculations for a four-card draw.

## The combo turn

The deck's "combo" is a two-card conversion in one turn:

1. Get Recursive Recruitment into the graveyard. Cryomancer, Sphinx of False Conclusions and Something Worth Saving all do
   it incidentally; you can also discard it to Twinned Vision's flashback cost.
2. Flash it back for `{6}{U}{B}` with twenty or more cards in the graveyard. Two Cadets enter with six or more `+1/+1`
   counters each, which is twelve power across two bodies in one turn with no prior board.
3. Copy the larger Cadet with Hall of Echoes for `{5}` and attack for the difference.

With Uldaros Theorix in the same turn, the flashback and the free-cast trigger can chain: Theorix exiles the Recruitment
from the graveyard as its sorcery, copies it, and casts the copy for free, which puts two more counters-scaled Cadets on
the board without paying the flashback cost.

## Win condition 2

When the graveyard is smaller, the deck wins with bodies. Tarmogoyf is a two-mana threat that is usually 4/5 or 5/6 by
turn four because instants, sorceries, creatures and lands are all in graveyards. Dark Matter Manipulator is a one-mana
threat that grows two power per seven cards. Winter, Tormented Loner is a 0/3 that edicts on entry and then attacks as a
five- or six-power creature once the graveyard fills. Hall of Echoes converts any of them into a second copy for a turn,
which is how the deck closes through a single blocker.

## Mulligan guide

| Hand | Keep? |
|---|---|
| One-drop Manipulator, two lands, a two-drop | Keep. The deck needs the engine online by turn two |
| Two lands, Cryomancer, Something Worth Saving, Recursive Recruitment | Keep. Twelve cards in the graveyard by turn four is the threshold that makes Recruitment lethal |
| All lands and Uldaros | Mulligan. Six mana with no mill is a dead hand |
| Chandra plus three lands and no mill | Keep on the play, mulligan on the draw. Chandra belongs in a hand that already mills |

## Key interactions and edge cases

- **Cruel Calculations targets a player.** Target yourself after milling to draw the full count; targeting the opponent
  only counts their own library-to-graveyard movement.
- **Tarmogoyf counts all graveyards.** Removal spells and fetch-style sacrifice effects on the other side of the table
  grow it too.
- **Chandra's first `+1` returns only noncreature, nonland cards.** Creature cards stay in the graveyard, which is where
  Winter and Recursive Recruitment want them.
- **Primal Witchstalker needs a land in the graveyard** for the second half of its trigger; it will whiff if the four
  milled cards are all spells.
- **Hall of Echoes produces colourless mana.** It is a fifth-land-plus card, not a turn-three land.
- **Darklight Phoenix needs two creatures to have died this turn.** It returns at the beginning of combat, so it is a
  rebuy after a block-heavy turn, not a turn-four play.
- **Sphinx of False Conclusions copies itself when it dies**, and the copy is a token, so it does not loop further but it
  does leave a 4/2 flier behind after a trade.

## Matchups

| Opponent | Plan |
|---|---|
| Aggro | Cryomancer's stun counters and Winter's edict are the whole plan; block with Manipulator and race with Goyf |
| Control | Force them to spend removal on Manipulator, then refill with Cryomancer and Chandra; Recursive Recruitment is best held until they tap out |
| Midrange | Grind with Sphinx recursion and Hall of Echoes copies; your threats cost less and scale harder |
| Combo | No interaction main deck. Mulligan toward the fastest mill curve and race with flying |

# Iterations

| Round | Change | Result |
|---|---|---|
| v1 | Initial build: 4 Dark Matter Manipulator, 4 Something Worth Saving, 4 Tarmogoyf, 3 Primal Witchstalker, 3 Seasoned Cryomancer, 1 Yuriko, 1 Last Gasp, 1 Cruel Calculations, 1 Darklight Phoenix, 24 lands | All gates pass: sim 54.3, synergy 73.0, T4 0.625, P(4 lands) 0.619 |
| v2 | -1 Yuriko, -1 Last Gasp, +1 Seasoned Cryomancer, +1 Cruel Calculations (more mill and card flow, less one-for-one interaction) | All gates pass: sim 55.7, synergy 73.6, T4 0.653, P(4 lands) 0.634 |
| v3 | -2 Cruel Calculations, +2 Last Gasp (tested interaction over velocity) | Rejected: sim fell to 46.0, list reverted to v2 |
